[merged-deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017-atleast2of3]
[final-deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017-effort-high-run1]
`:module.ec2_update_runner_ssm_ami` deploys a Lambda that reads/updates the runner AMI SSM parameters at `/github-action-runners/${prefix}/<runner>/runners/config/ami_id`, i.e. parameters owned and created by `:module.runners`. It currently depends only on `var.runner_configs`/`var.tenant_configs` (the ARNs are hand-built strings), so nothing orders it after the runners module and the Lambda's first GetParameter/PutParameter calls can hit parameters that don't exist yet. Contrast with `:module.ec2_update_runner_tags`, which is ordered implicitly because it consumes `module.runners.webhook.eventbridge.event_bus.name`. There is no attribute of `module.runners` to wire in here, so an explicit `depends_on = [module.runners]` is the appropriate fix.

----------------------------------------

[final-deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017-effort-high-run2]
`:module.ec2_update_runner_ssm_ami` builds the SSM parameter ARNs it manages from locally concatenated strings (`local.runner_ami_ssm_parameter_arns`) instead of from any resource or module, so it has no ordering relative to `:module.runners`, which owns/creates those `/github-action-runners/<prefix>/<runner_key>/runners/config/ami_id` parameters. On a fresh apply the scheduled lambda can be deployed and invoked (the rule fires every 10 minutes) while the parameters do not yet exist, so its GetParameter call fails. Add `depends_on = [module.runners]` on `:module.ec2_update_runner_ssm_ami`.

[merged-deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017-atleast2of3]
[final-deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017-effort-high-run2]
`:data.aws_ssm_parameter.ami_id` reads `/github-action-runners/<prefix>/<runner_key>/runners/config/ami_id`, a parameter that is created by `:module.runners` (the multi-runner module manages the runner config SSM parameters, and the AMI is later refreshed in place by the AMI-updater lambda). The read only references a locally-built name string (`local.runner_ami_ssm_parameter_names`), so the graph records no dependency and Terraform may refresh this data source during plan before the parameter exists, failing with ParameterNotFound on a fresh apply. `:data.aws_ssm_parameter.ami_id` should depend on `:module.runners` (e.g. a `depends_on = [module.runners]`), which also transitively fixes `:data.aws_ami.runner_ami`.

----------------------------------------

[final-deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017-effort-high-run3]
`data.aws_ssm_parameter.ami_id` reads `/github-action-runners/${var.runner_configs.prefix}/${key}/runners/config/ami_id`, but those parameters are created by `module.runners` (the multi-runner module's SSM runner-config parameters, enabled via `enable_ssm_on_runners = true`). Terraform sees no relationship between the two, so on a fresh apply the data source is read before the parameters exist and fails with ParameterNotFound. The data source should depend on `module.runners` (e.g. an explicit `depends_on`), since nothing about the parameter name can reference the module in a clean way.

----------------------------------------

[merged-glm-5.3-flash-atleast2of3]
[final-glm-5.3-flash-effort-high-run1]
data.aws_ssm_parameter.ami_id reads SSM parameters under /github-action-runners/<prefix>/<key>/runners/config/ami_id, which are created by module.runners (the terraform-aws-github-runner multi-runner module) at apply time. No attribute reference or depends_on establishes this ordering, so on a fresh apply the data read happens before the parameters exist and the apply fails; data.aws_ami.runner_ami and output.ec2_runners_ami_name_map fail transitively. Add an explicit depends_on on module.runners (no attribute of the data source can reference the module, so a data-dependency fix is not available).

----------------------------------------

[final-glm-5.3-flash-effort-high-run2]
data.aws_ssm_parameter.ami_id reads the runner-config SSM parameters (/github-action-runners/<prefix>/<key>/runners/config/ami_id) that are created by module.runners, but it has no attribute reference or depends_on linking it to the module. On a fresh environment the data read would evaluate before the parameters exist and fail with ParameterNotFound; an explicit depends_on on module.runners is needed to defer the read until after the parameters are created.

----------------------------------------

[final-glm-5.3-flash-effort-high-run3]
data.aws_ssm_parameter.ami_id reads the SSM parameters "/github-action-runners/<prefix>/<key>/runners/config/ami_id", which are created by module.runners (the terraform-aws-github-runner multi-runner module stores each runner group's AMI id there). There is no attribute reference or depends_on from this data source to module.runners, and the parameter names are computed purely from var.runner_configs, so Terraform reads the data source at plan time — on the first apply this fails hard with ParameterNotFound because module.runners has not created the parameters yet.
